edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.mechanism: Continuous positive airway pressure is plausibly linked to Cognitive function through mechanisms that fit its exposure class and target tissue, but the exact pathway depends on dose, timing, and baseline vulnerability. The best interpretation is usually that it changes the biologic setting in which Cognitive function develops rather than acting as a single on-off switch.
edges.summary: CPAP evidence is strongest for symptom relief and sleepiness; harder vascular or cognitive endpoints improve less consistently. Pooled meta-analytic evidence link continuous positive airway pressure to better cognitive function in adults with obstructive sleep apnea. The average effect is usually unknown rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
